newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS V MILAN - MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS V MILAN - MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Here is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Juventus and Milan who meet in Italy's serie A at the Stadio Delle Alpi on Sunday (1930 GMT):

Playing style: with the arrival of Frenchman Zinedine Zidane and Croat Alen Boksic, coach Marcello Lippi has refined the 4-3-3 formation that brought Juve the European Cup. The recent 5-0 Champions' League win over Rapid Vienna was the fruit of a 4-3-2-1 line-up, with the flair of Alessandro Del Piero -- back from injury -- and Zidane supplying targetman Boksic. But with three-quarters of his back four unavailable for the AC Milan match, Lippi may prefer a more conservative 4-4-2 with Michele Padovano and Boksic up front.

Strengths: Tactics. Juve's relentless harrying of opponents coupled with the ability to switch defence into attack is a threat from any part of the field. Lippi has won deserved praise for the ease with which Boksic and Zidane have settled into his system. A fierce training routine -- often likened to the U.S. Marines -- enables Juve to keep up their act for the full 90 minutes.

Weaknesses: Italy's Ciro Ferrara and Uruguayan Paolo Montero are both suspended and Gianluca Pessotto injured, so Lippi must redesign his back four. Expect 21-year-old Alessio Tacchinardi -- one full match this season -- to partner Sergio Porrini in the centre of the defence. Midfielder Angelo Di Livio may move back to cover the right-back spot with Moreno Torricelli on the left.

Motivation: Revenge. Juve lost league title to Milan last season and Lippi consistently points to championship as priority. In recent seasons, the winner of this clash has gone on to take title and a win would put Juventus five points clear of Milan.

Line-up (probably from): Angelo Peruzzi; Moreno Torricelli, Angelo Di Livio, Alessio Tacchinardi, Sergio Porrini, Mark Iuliano; Didier Deschamps, Vladimir Jugovic, Zinedine Zidane, Alessandro Del Piero; Michele Padovano, Alen Boksic, Christian Vieri.

Playing style: Uruguayan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez started season with 4-3-3 to accommodate Roberto Baggio and Dejan Savicevic in same side. Worst start in years swiftly saw Baggio relegated to sub's bench and a return to 4-4-2 system that gave ex-manager Fabio Capello four titles in five years.

But current side is shadow of Capello's team. The offside trap and "pressing" Capello used to stifle opponents have gone as has the machine-like efficiency that united the club's talented parts into a whole.

Strengths: Innate understanding between George Weah and Marco Simone that produced four goals against Gothenburg in Champions' League. Fans have warmed to Baggio's return to form with five goals from subs bench. In midfield Tabarez has successfully blooded youngsters Tomas Locatelli and Massimo Ambrosini while tenacious Edgar Davids, signed from Ajax, has become a regular.

Weaknesses: Defence. Milan are conceding a goal a game. Real spanner in red-and-black machine is absence of 36-year-old Franco Baresi with injury. Without "Kaiser Franz", both Paolo Maldini and Alessandro Costacurta look ill at ease. To shore up defence, Marcel Desailly has moved back from midfield but shifting the Frenchman from his usual midfield holding role is like retreating your last line of defence.

Motivation: with a league title to defend and a probable clash with Juventus in European Cup quarter-finals next February, Milan do not lack motivation. But indifferent performances with virtually the same side that has dominated serie A for five years suggests team's appetite for success is on wane. Hence Tabarez's injection of fresh blood.

Line-up (probably from): Sebastiano Rossi; Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi, Marcel Desailly, Alessandro Costacurta, Michael Reiziger; Demetrio Albertini, Zvonimir Boban, Edgar Davids, Stefanio Eranio, Tomas Locatelli, Dejan Savicevic, George Weah, Marco Simone, Roberto Baggio.
